rationale:
`requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.fn` only declares a signature: `Sources::search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>`, and it is async. It states no runtime behavior beyond the doc line "Search available project files." The behavior and inputs are in the sibling requirements `search_text.behavior` and `search_text.inputs`, which are not the subject here.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` calls `sources.search_text(&TextQuery::new(..))` on a `Sources` value and awaits it. It unwraps the `Ok` result and reads `.complete` and `.matches`, including `.path`, so it uses the `TextMatches` shape. It also asserts `.is_err()` for the `SourceScope::under("..")` query, which exercises the `Err` side of the result type. The test would not compile if the signature differed in receiver, query type, async-ness or result type.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` exercises the `search_text` tool through the session. That is an additional, indirect use of the function. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.

text: pub async fn search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>;
